gaps.sentence: The match was abandoned ___ the state of the pitch.
gaps.explanation: 'Owing to + noun' = because of, common in formal reporting.

gaps.sentence: Scarcely had she opened the letter ___ she burst into tears.
gaps.explanation: 'Scarcely... when' marks the immediate consequence of the first event.

gaps.sentence: I can't afford a holiday this year; ___, I can't get the time off work.
gaps.explanation: 'Besides' adds a further, often decisive, reason in informal style.

gaps.sentence: She earns a very good salary; ___, she never seems to have any money.
gaps.explanation: 'Yet' contrasts two facts, like but, in a slightly more formal way.

gaps.sentence: ___ they promise rapid results, such diets rarely work.
gaps.explanation: 'Although' introduces the clause 'they promise rapid results'.

gaps.sentence: The scheme creates hundreds of jobs. ___, it attracts tourism to the region.
gaps.explanation: 'In addition' introduces another benefit of the scheme.

gaps.sentence: I enjoyed the film; the ending was weak, ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Though' can come at the end of a sentence as a casual contrast marker; the others cannot.

gaps.sentence: Nobody volunteered to stay late, ___ Tomas.
gaps.explanation: 'Apart from Tomas' = except for Tomas, the only person who volunteered.
